stem: When crystals of copper sulphate are strongly heated, the residue obtained is ______.
solution: When crystals of copper sulphate (blue, hydrated) are strongly heated, the water of crystallisation is driven off and the anhydrous residue obtained is colourless (white). Correct option: (d) colourless.

stem: Which type of mirror is used by a dentist?
solution: Dentists use a concave mirror in order to obtain a large (magnified) image of the teeth. Correct option: (c) Concave.

stem: The equivalent resistance of the parallel combination of two resistors of \(60\ \Omega\) and \(40\ \Omega\) is ______.
solution: For a parallel combination, \(\dfrac{1}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{R_1} + \dfrac{1}{R_2} = \dfrac{1}{60} + \dfrac{1}{40} = 0.041\). Therefore \(R_{eq} = \dfrac{1}{0.041} = 24\ \Omega\). Correct option: (a) \(24\ \Omega\).

stem: The litmus paper or the litmus solution is obtained from ______ plant.
solution: Litmus paper or litmus solution is obtained from lichens. Correct option: (b) Lichen.

subtopic: Acids and Bases in Daily Life
stem: Which substance when used with butter having butyric acid can cure acidity?
solution: Lime water, being basic, when used with butter having butyric acid can neutralise the acidity. Correct option: (a) Lime water.

subtopic: Early Attempts and Mendeleev's Periodic Table
stem: State Newland's law of octaves.
solution: Newland's law of octaves: When elements are arranged in the increasing order of their atomic masses, the properties of every eighth element are similar to those of the first.

stem: State the right hand thumb rule.
solution: Right-hand thumb rule: Imagine that you are holding a current-carrying straight conductor in your right hand such that the thumb points towards the direction of the current. Then your fingers will wrap around the conductor in the direction of the magnetic field lines.

stem: If a bulb of 60 W is connected across a source of 220 V, find the current drawn by it.
solution:
Given: Power of the bulb \(P = 60\ \mathrm{W}\), P.D. across the bulb \(V = 220\ \mathrm{V}\).
Using \(P = V \times I\):
\(60 = 220 \times I\)
\(I = \dfrac{60}{220} = 0.27\ \mathrm{A}\).

subtopic: Human Eye and Defects of Vision
stem: Draw a neat and labelled diagram of the structure of the human eye.
solution: The labelled diagram of the human eye should show the following parts: Cornea, Iris, Pupil, Aqueous humour, Crystalline lens, Ciliary muscles, Vitreous humour, Retina and Optic nerve.

stem: Define: Radius of curvature of a spherical mirror.
solution: The radius of curvature (R) of a spherical mirror is the radius of the hollow sphere of glass of which the spherical mirror is a part.

stem: Define: Focal length of a spherical mirror.
solution: The focal length of a spherical mirror is the distance between its pole (P) and its principal focus (F).

stem: Give scientific reason: The sun appears reddish early in the morning.
solution: During sunrise (and sunset), sunlight has to travel a greater distance through the Earth's atmosphere to reach our eyes. Over this longer path, most of the shorter-wavelength blue light is scattered away and mainly the longer-wavelength red light reaches our eyes directly. Hence the Sun appears reddish early in the morning.

stem: Write the merits of the modern periodic table over Mendeleev's periodic table.
solution:
Merits of the modern periodic table over Mendeleev's periodic table:
(i) All isotopes of the same element have different masses but the same atomic number; hence they occupy the same position in the modern periodic table.
(ii) Elements are classified according to their electronic configuration into four blocks: s-block, p-block, d-block and f-block.
(iii) In the modern periodic table the elements are arranged according to their atomic numbers; therefore the anomaly of elements such as cobalt and nickel in Mendeleev's periodic table disappears.

stem: What is a redox reaction? Explain with one example.
solution:
A redox reaction is a chemical reaction in which oxidation and reduction take place simultaneously.
Example: \(\mathrm{CuO + H_2 \rightarrow Cu + H_2O}\). Here \(\mathrm{H_2}\) is oxidised to \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) (so \(\mathrm{H_2}\) is the reducing agent) and \(\mathrm{CuO}\) is reduced to \(\mathrm{Cu}\) (so \(\mathrm{CuO}\) is the oxidising agent). Since oxidation and reduction occur together, it is a redox reaction.

stem: What is resistivity? Write the formula of resistivity. Write the SI unit of resistivity.
solution:
Resistivity of a substance is numerically equal to the resistance of a rod of that substance which is 1 metre long and 1 square metre in cross-section.
Formula: \(\rho = R\dfrac{A}{l}\), where \(R\) is the resistance, \(A\) is the area of cross-section and \(l\) is the length of the wire.
SI unit of resistivity: ohm metre \((\Omega\cdot\mathrm{m})\).

stem: Distinguish between degradable pollutants and non-degradable pollutants (any three points).
solution:
| Degradable pollutants | Non-degradable pollutants |
|---|---|
| 1. They can degrade on their own over a period of time. | 1. They cannot degrade on their own. |
| 2. They are acted upon by microorganisms and are converted to inorganic substances. | 2. They are not acted upon by microorganisms and so exist in the complex form only. |
| 3. They do not get accumulated in nature. | 3. They get accumulated in nature and persist for a long time. |
| 4. They emit foul odour when they are being decomposed. | 4. They do not emit foul odour as they are not decomposed. |
| 5. Examples: Vegetables, fruits, organic matter. | 5. Examples: Metals, plastic, glass. |

subtopic: Human Eye and Defects of Vision
context: Kavita from 10th standard is using spectacles. The power of the lenses in her spectacles is \(-2.5\) dioptre.
stem: State the defect of vision Kavita is suffering from.
solution: A concave lens is used to correct the defect called myopia. Hence, Kavita is suffering from myopia (short-sightedness).

context: Kavita from 10th standard is using spectacles. The power of the lenses in her spectacles is \(-2.5\) dioptre.
stem: Find the focal length of the lenses used in her spectacles.
solution:
Power of a lens \(P = \dfrac{1}{f\ (\text{in metres})}\).
Therefore \(f = \dfrac{1}{P} = \dfrac{1}{-2.5} = -0.4\ \mathrm{m} = -40\ \mathrm{cm}\).
Thus the focal length of the lens is 40 cm (the negative sign indicates a concave lens). [Booklet states the magnitude 0.4 m = 40 cm, omitting the negative sign.]

stem: Write the chemical name of bleaching powder and write its properties.
solution:
The molecular formula of bleaching powder is \(\mathrm{CaOCl_2}\) and its chemical name is calcium oxychloride.
Properties:
(i) Bleaching powder is a yellowish-white coloured solid substance.
(ii) Its chemical name is calcium oxychloride.
(iii) It has a strong odour of chlorine gas.
(iv) Dilute sulphuric acid and dilute hydrochloric acid react rapidly with bleaching powder to release chlorine gas completely: \(\mathrm{CaOCl_2 + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow CaSO_4 + Cl_2\uparrow + H_2O}\).

stem: Explain the construction and working of an electric motor.
solution:
Construction of an electric motor:
- The electric motor consists of a rectangular coil ABCD of insulated copper wire mounted between the poles of a horseshoe magnet so that it can freely rotate between the N and S poles. The coil along with the magnet is called the armature.
- A device called the commutator or split ring reverses the current.
- There are carbon brushes B1 and B2 fixed at the base of the motor.

Working of an electric motor:
- The rectangular coil is placed in the magnetic field and current is passed through it. Thus, a force acts on it and it causes the motor to rotate continuously.
- The commutator reverses the direction of current flowing through the coil every time the coil passes the vertical position during a revolution.
- The carbon brushes make contact with the rotating rings of the commutator and then supply the current to the coil.
- The rotating shaft of the electric motor can drive a large number of machines which are connected to it.

stem: What is refraction of light? Draw the diagram of refraction of light in a glass slab. Write the laws of refraction.
solution:
Refraction of light: The phenomenon of change in the path of light while going from one medium to another is called refraction of light.

Laws of refraction:
(i) The incident ray, the refracted ray and the normal to the interface of the two media at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.
(ii) The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant for a given pair of media: \(\dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \text{constant} = {}^{1}n_{2}\). This law is also known as Snell's law. The constant \({}^{1}n_{2}\) is called the refractive index of the second medium (in which the refracted ray lies) with respect to the first medium (in which the incident ray lies).
